name: Hertz–Branly signal trials
summary: Marconi's first trials combining Hertz's spark transmitter with Branly's filings detector in an attempt to send telegraph signals without wires.
description: An ordinary Hertz oscillator and Branly coherer are combined in preliminary tests aimed at transmitting telegraphic signs without connecting wires.
tier_reason: Fine historical detail or an evidentiary witness; retention supports explanation without claiming broad later dependence.
why: Laboratory demonstrations of electrical waves suggested to Marconi that they could carry telegraph signals.

links.statement: Marconi reports using a Branly coherer alongside the Hertz oscillator, then changing the filings detector because the initial version was unreliable.
links.alternatives: Hertz’s laboratory observations used a spark-gap detector; Marconi’s recorded trials use a conductive-contact detector instead.
links.caveats: Marconi’s later account supports his component use; it does not by itself settle all coherer priority disputes.

links.statement: Marconi reports beginning his signalling trials with an ordinary Hertz oscillator, adapting a laboratory wave source to a communications objective.
links.alternatives: Marconi subsequently tried a Righi oscillator with reflectors, as the same lecture records.
links.caveats: The report identifies the oscillator design tradition, not the physical reuse of Hertz’s own instrument or an exact replication of every dimension.
links.timing: The receiving development follows the source development.
